provenance_events.description: The 116500LN puts a black Cerachrom bezel on the steel Daytona, visually recalling the 6241 of the 1960s and immediately dating the outgoing 116520. The watch trades at a sustained premium for its entire 2016-2023 production run.

Rolex replaces the 116500LN with the 126500LN in March 2023, moving to a new movement and a subtly redesigned case. The 116500LN becomes the reference collectors cite when talking about the 2016-2022 waitlist era.

Rolex launches the 116500LN at Baselworld 2016 — the first steel Daytona with a ceramic bezel since the 116520. The release is a watershed for Asian collectors, with multi-year waitlists at ADs in Hong Kong, Singapore, and Tokyo by end of 2016.

narrative.story: Rolex put a black Cerachrom bezel on the steel Daytona in 2016, visually recalling the black-bezel 6241 of the 1960s and immediately dating the outgoing 116520. Demand outran supply for its entire seven-year run: authorized dealers kept multi-year lists and the watch traded at a large premium over retail throughout, peaking in early 2022. Discontinued in 2023 for the 126500LN, it remains the shorthand example of the retail-versus-grey-market gap.
narrative.collector_notes: White 'panda' dials carry a consistent premium over black. Check the bezel edge for chips and the warranty-card date; 2023-dated full sets mark the final production year.
